newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Lobo gold project seen at 300,000 oz/yr.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Lobo gold project seen at 300,000 oz/yr.

text.p: Canada's Teck Corp and Chile's Empresa Minera de Mantos Blancos expect their gold joint venture called Lobo-Marte to produce between 275,000 and 300,000 ounces per year, said officials of both companies.
The mine will produce gold for a cash cost of $220 an ounce, Teck President Norman Keevil told a news conference.
Construction on the previously-announced project will begin in December 1997 subject to completion of feasibility studies and obtaining local permits, he said.
The Lobo-Marte project will be developed by a new company called Santa Rosa, which will be owned 60 percent by Teck Gold Ltd and 40 percent by Mantos Blancos, officials said.
The deposit is located in the Maricunga gold belt in Chile's Third Region at 4,000 meters above sea level.
